meeting_header:
Date: 2026-06-03 | Time: 15:00 - 15:38 UTC | Duration: 38m
Attendees: Jamie Torres (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Oliver Reed (Celestia CTO), Priya Singh (Celestia ML Eng), Marcus Li (Celestia Platform)
summary: Redwood hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming responses, tunable params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), and retry/backoff behavior. Customer (Celestia Commerce) is evaluating options for a POC to power conversational product recommendations. Key concerns: latency at scale, cost tradeoffs, SSO/security, and on-prem vs hosted. Agreed next steps around pricing, security docs, and POC scoping.
topics: Parameters: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences
SDK and quickstart, rate limits and quotas
Security/compliance questions: SOC2, KMS, data retention
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Torres: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick intro i'm jamie from Redwood, with me is maya our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Oliver Reed: hey jamie, thanks - i'm oliver, cto at celestia commerce. Priya and Marcus are here too.
[00:20] Priya Singh: hey all, excited to see the demo.
[00:28] Maya Patel: cool, so agenda - quick questions about your use case, then i'll walk through Hosted API demo, streaming, params, and retries, and then we'll chat about p o c.
[00:40] Marcus Li: sounds good. our main goal is to embed conversation-based product recs on checkout, need low latency and predictable cost.
[00:52] Jamie Torres: perfect, are you leaning hosted or dedicated?
[00:57] Oliver Reed: we'd prefer hosted to start, but if latency or residency becomes an issue we may look at dedicated or private.
[01:06] Maya Patel: makes sense. quick Q: what's your current traffic pattern?
[01:10] Priya Singh: peak 60 requests per second, average 20, but bursts to 120 during promos.
[01:18] Maya Patel: ok that's helpful - we'll demo batching, streaming and how to configure retries for those bursts.
[01:30] Maya Patel: demo screen share: (link deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/hosted-api-demo) - first, simple chat API call.
[01:42] Maya Patel: so here's a standard POST chat.complete request - messages array, model param, temperature etc. note we support streaming over server-sent events and ws-ish streaming in our SDKs.
[02:05] Priya Singh: streaming - how does that affect latency?
[02:10] Maya Patel: good question; streaming returns tokens as they're generated, so perceived latency to the user drops significantly; total compute is similar but UX is better. also you can early render partials.
[02:24] Oliver Reed: does streaming increase request concurrency or hold connections?
[02:29] Maya Patel: it holds the connection open longer but per-token throughput is efficient. we have connection pooling recommendations and auto timeouts; for heavy bursts we recommend a mix of batching and streaming for front-end fast responses.
[02:45] Marcus Li: what's the default timeout? we saw a 15s in docs.
[02:49] Maya Patel: defaults vary by plan; for hosted api default is 60s server-side, but client SDKs have keepalive timeouts you can tune.
[03:03] Maya Patel: next: generation params - temperature, top_p, max_tokens, presence/ frequency penalties, and stop sequences. here's a demo changing temperature from 0.2 to 0.8.
[03:18] (demo) [typing sounds]
[03:28] Maya Patel: low temp deterministic, high temp more creative - for product recs you probably want lower temp ~0.0-0.4 to reduce hallucinations.
[03:40] Priya Singh: noted, we care about hallucination for price or SKU references.
[03:45] Jamie Torres: you can also supply retrieval context or embeddings to ground answers, reduces hallucinations and cost if you do reranking.
[03:55] Oliver Reed: oh can you talk about retries? sometimes our front-end will retry on timeouts which has caused duplicated charges elsewhere.
[04:03] Maya Patel: yes so Redwood's API returns an idempotency token header if you send one, and we have recommended retry semantics - exponential backoff, jitter. we also provide a request-id in responses for tracing.
[04:18] Priya Singh: is idempotency automatic or do we have to generate client-side?
[04:22] Maya Patel: best practice is client-generated idempotency keys for create-like calls. for chat turns it's safe to be idempotent at the message level if you store client-turn ids.
[04:34] Marcus Li: how do you handle partial responses on retries? like we got partial stream then retry.
[04:40] Maya Patel: good edge case - you should checkpoint the last successful token offset, use the idempotency key and request the remaining tokens; our SDKs expose resume helpers. there can be small duplication unless you dedupe at the UI layer.
[04:56] Oliver Reed: hmm okay. do you support automatic retry on network error in the SDK?
[05:01] Maya Patel: yes; default SDK has retry with backoff for idempotent operations, and you can disable or tune it. non-idempotent ops are not retried by default.
[05:12] Jamie Torres: also, for cost controls, you can set per-route quotas and token limits - that helps prevent runaway retries blowing budget.
[05:24] Priya Singh: show us streaming + stop sequences?
[05:28] Maya Patel: demo: set stop sequence to ["\n\nUser:"] so the model stops when it hits system prompt - see streaming stops immediately.
[05:40] (partial transcript: audio glitch)
[05:46] Maya Patel: (continuing) there was a small audio blip, sorry - but you can chain stop tokens and also set max_tokens to cap cost.
[05:56] Oliver Reed: do you offer server-side caching for prompts? we have many repeated system prompts.
[06:02] Maya Patel: yes - prefix/KV caching is supported on certain models; it caches decoder key-value for repeated prefixes which reduces compute on repeated flows.
[06:14] Marcus Li: any limits on cache size or TTL?
[06:17] Maya Patel: TTL configurable per route; cache size depends on model and plan, we'll share recommended settings.
[06:27] Jamie Torres: switching to SDKs - we have Python, Node, and go examples. (link: https://redwood.ai/sdk)
[06:35] Maya Patel: here's a Node example for streaming using EventSource. quickstart is two commands, and you get streaming with a couple lines.
[06:46] Priya Singh: do you have a React example for progressive rendering?
[06:49] Maya Patel: yep, we have a small reference app that does token-by-token rendering - i'll include the link in follow-up.
[06:58] Oliver Reed: security - we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS integration. what's supported?
[07:07] Jamie Torres: we are SOC2 Type II certified, support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, and we integrate with major KMS providers for customer-managed keys. security whitepaper: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf
[07:23] Priya Singh: does hosted store PII? we need data residency controls.
[07:28] Maya Patel: hosted option can be configured with retention policies; by default we don't use customer data to train underlying models, and you can enable deletion hooks. for residency we have region selection - US/EU hubs - and if you need VPC/private we can discuss Private deployments.
[07:44] Marcus Li: performance - can you run a quick latency test with our numbers?
[07:49] Maya Patel: sure, i'll mock 50 rps with 256-token prompts, show batch sizing effect. (demo run)
[08:05] Maya Patel: results: single-shot non-batched median p95 ~220ms per request on our curated 7B model; with batching throughput increases but p95 tail can increase if you allow larger batches.
[08:18] Oliver Reed: 220ms is good. what about 99th percentile under burst?
[08:23] Maya Patel: under bursts p99 can hit 700-900ms on hosted default unless you use Dedicated pools or route to a lower-cost variant; we also have automatic fallback policies to route overflow to compatible variants.
[08:36] Priya Singh: pricing question - how are streaming tokens billed vs non-streaming?
[08:42] Jamie Torres: billed per generated token regardless of streaming; input tokens billed similarly. there are also token rounding rules and min-bills for very small responses - we'll send the pricing sheet.
[08:53] Oliver Reed: Any guidance on temperature for recommendation use-cases? you said 0.0-0.4. what about sampling + rerank?
[09:00] Maya Patel: for recommendations we recommend low temp plus n-best sampling then rerank with embeddings or heuristic scoring - reduces hallucination and lets you control diversity.
[09:12] Marcus Li: do you have a built-in reranking tool?
[09:15] Maya Patel: we provide utilities in Redwood Optimize for candidate scoring and we can export logs for offline rerank experiments. Optimize also suggests quantization and batching params to reduce cost.
[09:27] Jamie Torres: noted we also offer per-route cost dashboards so product team can see token-level spend.
[09:34] (short silence)
[09:40] Priya Singh: about retries again - if client retries, do you have server-side dedupe for idempotency key collisions?
[09:46] Maya Patel: yes, we check idempotency keys and return the same response for the same key when appropriate; we also store request metadata for replay protection.
[09:56] Oliver Reed: what's retention on those logs? we need 12 months for audit.
[09:59] Jamie Torres: audit logs retention is configurable, enterprise plans support 12+ months; we'll include specifics in the security doc.
[10:10] Marcus Li: onboarding - how long to spin up and are there SDK keys per environment?
[10:14] Jamie Torres: you can self-serve sign-up and get API keys, environment-level keys recommended; Dedicated/private onboarding typically 4-6 weeks depending on infra.
[10:25] Priya Singh: do you support per-team RBAC?
[10:27] Maya Patel: yes we have RBAC, SSO groups via SCIM, and per-route ACLs for team isolation.
[10:36] Oliver Reed: ok we're about to run a POC. timeline target: have basic POC by end of June and evaluation by mid-July.
[10:44] Jamie Torres: great - proposed POC: 2-week pilot, use hosted API with a curated 7B model, sample throughput 50 rps, run bench and UX test.
[10:55] Maya Patel: action items: i will run cost/latency estimate for 50 rps and 120 burst, jamie will send pricing and security doc, oliver to share sample prompts.
[11:08] (crosstalk) Priya Singh: can you also include the react progressive render example?
[11:12] Maya Patel: yes - link will be in the follow-up.
[11:18] Oliver Reed: any blockers on our side? we have strict procurement but this should be a standard SaaS contract.
[11:24] Jamie Torres: we can share a standard MSA and SOW template; procurement often asks for addendum for data handling - we have previous templates.
[11:34] Marcus Li: one last question: are there built-in rate limit headers to help client backoff?
[11:39] Maya Patel: yes we return X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and Retry-After on 429s; SDK has helpers to do smart backoff.
[11:50] Oliver Reed: ok that's helpful.
[11:54] Jamie Torres: cool - recap: we'll send pricing & SOC2, maya will run latency/cost numbers, set POC scoping call for Jun 10. anything else?
[12:05] Priya Singh: include sample token distribution template - i'll fill it out.
[12:09] Oliver Reed: thanks everyone, we'll review and get back.
[12:13] Jamie Torres: thanks - we'll follow up shortly.
[12:18] (end)
